title: 7 Email Finding Tools Compared: Pricing, Credits and Best Uses
summary: Compare Hunter, Apollo, Snov.io and other email finding tools with checked pricing, credit rules and a practical test for your outbound team.
body_markdown:
Use Hunter when you already know the person and company. Evaluate Apollo when you need to build the prospect list as well as find the addresses. If your team already has an outreach platform, compare a dedicated finder before buying another prospecting seat.


An email lookup and an annual sales-platform seat can appear under the same “starting price” label. Compare what the plan buys before comparing the price.


Below are seven options, what each is useful for, and the billing detail to check before paying. Public prices and product pages were checked on **October 23, 2026** . Prices are in US dollars; annual billing is labeled explicitly.


## Email finding tools: the shortlist


Start with the row that matches the work your team actually needs to do. The table compares entry offers, not equivalent quantities of usable contacts.


Tool


Best for


Public entry offer


Free option


Buying detail

## Hunter: best for a list of people you already know


Reps can look up a named person or inspect the addresses associated with a target company.[Email Finder accepts a full name and company email domain](https://hunter.io/email-finder) ; Domain Search supports the company-level route.


Hunter combines publicly discovered addresses with name-pattern inference and verification. When an address has been found publicly, the result can include[source URLs and discovery dates](https://hunter.io/email-finder) . That gives a rep something to inspect when an address looks wrong, rather than just another database record. Bulk CSV, Google Sheets and API workflows are available.


[Starter costs $49 month to month for 2,000 credits, with unlimited team members sharing the pool](https://hunter.io/pricing) .[A found email uses one credit; a search with no result uses none](https://hunter.io/pricing) . Separately requested verification uses[0.5 credit per email](https://hunter.io/pricing) . Monthly credits do not roll over, so size the plan around work you will actually complete during the billing period.


Run your existing account list through the bulk workflow and inspect the returned statuses before export. A confidence score on an unvalidated result is not the same thing as the green Verified status described in[Hunter's FAQ](https://hunter.io/email-finder) .


## Apollo: best when you also need to find the people


A rep can move from a buyer-profile search into a sequence without first assembling a separate name-and-domain file.[Apollo bundles contact and account data with prospecting, sequences and enrichment](https://www.apollo.io/pricing) . Test the handoff from prospect filter to CRM record to sequence to see whether it removes the rep’s manual CSV export and import step.


[Basic is $49 per seat per month billed annually, with 30,000 credits per seat per year granted upfront](https://www.apollo.io/pricing) . Those credits support multiple platform activities; they are not a promise of the same number of email addresses. Unused credits expire at the end of the billing cycle.


The main purchasing constraint is team-wide plan selection:[all seats on an account must use the same plan](https://www.apollo.io/pricing) . Work out which reps actually need prospecting and sequencing access before comparing its cost with a shared finder subscription.


Test the complete route from prospect filters to a CRM record and sequence. If that removes work your reps currently do elsewhere, include the replaced subscription in the buying decision. If you only need enrichment, compare that task separately.


## Snov.io: best for finding and sending in one subscription


Add colleagues without adding a separate paid seat for each person.[Starter includes unlimited team seats, 1,000 credits and 5,000 recipients for $39 on monthly billing](https://snov.io/pricing) . The annual offer is[$29.25 per month effective](https://snov.io/pricing) .


The important distinction is between credits and recipients.[Finder and Verifier share the credit pool, and each prospect or email verification costs one credit](https://snov.io/pricing) . Recipients measure leads first contacted during the billing period. Do not add the advertised finding and verification quantities together as though both were separate allowances.


The free plan is useful for checking the interface, but not the full export workflow:[Trial excludes export, bulk search, bulk verification, integrations and API access](https://snov.io/pricing) . Use a paid pilot if the buying decision depends on moving a real list into your CRM.


Before subscribing, map which actions spend credits and which spend recipients. Confirm the cost of any LinkedIn workflow separately, since[LinkedIn automation slots are not included in Sales Suite pricing](https://snov.io/pricing) .


## Anymail Finder: best for paying against verified search results


Use Anymail Finder when you want to enrich named contacts without buying prospecting seats. A person search accepts a name and company/domain, or a LinkedIn URL, and[uses one credit only when a verified email is found](https://anymailfinder.com/pricing) . Verification is included in the result.


The public monthly plans start at[$29 for 400 credits or $49 for 1,000 credits](https://anymailfinder.com/pricing) . Unlimited team members share the allowance. Credits roll over without a cap while subscribed; after cancellation they expire at the end of the current billing period.


The trial needs an explicit owner:[its 100 credits last seven days, require a card, and convert to a paid plan unless canceled](https://anymailfinder.com/pricing) . Put that cancellation decision on the calendar when starting the test.


For a list you already have, compare person-search results with separately checking the addresses already in your CRM. Those are different jobs:[verification of an existing email costs 0.2 credits per check](https://anymailfinder.com/pricing) . Preserve the lookup date in your export so later users know when the result was checked.


## Findymail: best for evaluating catch-all coverage


Run unresolved contacts through its catch-all checks and compare the additional usable addresses with your existing provider.[Findymail includes catch-all verification, bulk CSV enrichment, Google Sheets and API access](https://www.findymail.com/pricing) . The vendor publishes a[below-5% bounce-rate guarantee with credit refunds if the rate is higher](https://www.findymail.com/pricing) .


Read the plan type carefully.[Individual costs $99/month for one seat; Team costs $399/month for five seats](https://www.findymail.com/pricing) . These are usage-based prospecting plans, and the public page does not state an absolute Individual usage allowance. Ask for that allowance in writing before deciding whether it covers your batch.


A separate[credit-based Starter offer displays $99/month for 5,000 Finder Credits plus 5,000 bonus Verifier Credits](https://www.findymail.com/pricing) , positioned for reselling data or embedding it in a product. Do not apply that credit quota to the Individual plan.


Ask the vendor to show how your own CSV would be processed and which offer applies to that workflow. Judge catch-all results against current employment and delivery outcomes, not just whether a different verifier agrees with the label.


## LeadMagic: best for an API-led enrichment workflow


Add finding and validation as steps in the system that already prepares your outreach lists. Founder Jesse Ouellette's[published product comparison lists plans from $99/month for 5,000 credits, with one credit charged per valid work email found](https://leadmagic.io/blog/best-email-finder-tools) . Misses are not billed.


The same source documents a REST API and integrations with Clay, Apollo, Instantly and Smartlead. Separate validation costs[0.25 credit per definitive result; Unknown is not billed](https://leadmagic.io/blog/best-email-finder-tools) . Budget for separate validation when your list contains many old CRM addresses that need checking rather than finding.


Check the email status value in the API response and confirm that your automation keeps a miss out of the send list before buying for a recurring job.


The limit is scope:[LeadMagic is not a sequencer or CRM](https://leadmagic.io/blog/best-email-finder-tools) . Keep the cost of those systems in the comparison if you are building the outbound stack from scratch.


## Mailmeteor: best for a manual lookup without an account


Enter a full name and company domain in the public form to retrieve an address and its status.[Mailmeteor makes individual manual lookups free without signup, a credit card or a daily quota](https://mailmeteor.com/tools/email-finder) .


Its limitation is the workflow:[fair-use restrictions prevent automated scraping](https://mailmeteor.com/tools/email-finder) . The page invites inquiries about a bulk enrichment API, but does not publish its price. Do not budget recurring bulk work as though it were covered by the free lookup form.


Keep[Valid, Risky and Not Found](https://mailmeteor.com/tools/email-finder) results separate. Mailmeteor explains that Risky can reflect a catch-all domain or a mail server rate-limiting verification. A returned address alone is not enough reason to put that contact into a sequence.


## Compare the credit rules, not just the monthly price


Budget for the operations your list needs, including verification of addresses already in your CRM.[Hunter charges 0.5 credit for a separately requested verification](https://hunter.io/pricing) , while[Snov.io charges one credit per verification from its shared allowance](https://snov.io/pricing) . Their entry plans also include different amounts of credit and different outreach features.


For an already-enriched CRM export, ask what checking the existing addresses costs. For a name-only file, ask what finding an address costs and whether verification is included. Do not purchase a verification allowance to solve a missing-address problem.


Unused capacity matters too.[Hunter's monthly credits do not roll over](https://hunter.io/pricing) ;[Anymail Finder's credits accumulate while subscribed](https://anymailfinder.com/pricing) . Choose against the cadence of your actual list building, especially if outbound happens in account-based batches rather than every day.


## Test on your own target accounts before committing


Buy against results from your target accounts, not a vendor's headline accuracy percentage. Use current contacts from the accounts your reps are trying to reach, keeping the name and domain inputs identical across providers. Include the smaller companies and regions in your pipeline rather than testing only recognizable executives.


Keep the original contact row and add these fields to the export:


-


Provider, plan and lookup date.


-


Returned address, result status and credits consumed.


-


Evidence that the person still holds the relevant job at that company.


-


Whether the address duplicates another result or was already in your CRM.


-


Export or CRM-sync problems and the time needed to resolve them.


-


Delivery outcome for contacts your team actually emails.


Calculate **usable-contact coverage** as unique, current-employee contacts with an address your team accepts for sending, divided by eligible input contacts. Record what statuses your team accepts before comparing providers so a looser label does not win by default.


Calculate **cost per usable contact** as actual pilot spend divided by those usable contacts. For an existing subscription, track the credits consumed as well as any incremental cash spent. This keeps spare subscription capacity from looking like an infinitely free source of data.


Keep hard bounces separate from coverage: divide hard-bounced addresses by unique addresses attempted in your send. A verifier's acceptance label is not an observed delivery result, and no bounce does not establish inbox placement. Send only the contacts that pass your normal outreach checks, then record what happened.


## Add another finder only if it fills a measured gap


A second finder earns its place when it supplies usable contacts the first one missed. Send only unresolved contacts to the fallback, deduplicate the combined output, and compare the extra spend with the extra accepted contacts.


Include orchestration in the bill.[Clay orchestrates multiple providers rather than acting as a single email finder](https://leadmagic.io/blog/best-email-finder-tools) ; an orchestration subscription belongs in the cost calculation alongside the data providers it calls.


Before adding another provider, check the failed inputs.[Hunter's troubleshooting guidance names the wrong company email domain, misspelled names and people who have left the company](https://hunter.io/email-finder) . Another lookup cannot repair a target list nobody has kept current.


## Questions to settle before loading a sequence


### What is the difference between finding and verifying an email?


A finder starts with a person or company and returns an address. A verifier starts with an address you already have and checks it.[Hunter describes verification as part of its finding process](https://hunter.io/email-finder) , but a later check of an old CRM address is a separate task with its own credit rules.


### Can I send to catch-all results?


Keep them outside the main send list until your team has a basis for accepting them. A catch-all server accepts arbitrary recipient addresses, so[SMTP acceptance alone does not establish that the individual mailbox exists](https://leadmagic.io/blog/best-email-finder-tools) . Ask providers what additional checks produce their final status, and retain that status when exporting.


### Do free tools work for a team?


Use them to inspect results before paying, then test the handoff the team needs.[Snov.io's free Trial cannot export](https://snov.io/pricing) ;[Mailmeteor's free interface is for manual individual lookups](https://mailmeteor.com/tools/email-finder) . A free search that cannot enter your workflow may still leave a rep doing the data entry.


### Does a found work address give me permission to email?


No. Buying data does not settle the rules for sending to it.[Mailmeteor's own guidance calls for compliance with applicable outreach laws and honoring opt-outs](https://mailmeteor.com/tools/email-finder) . Apply your suppression list before export and have the person responsible for compliance approve the markets and outreach method.
